issues.evidence: The Federal Reserve's official 18 November 2026 press release states that the October 27–28 FOMC minutes were released at 2:00 p.m. EST. On that date EST was UTC−5, so publication was 19:00 UTC / 16:00 Brasília time, 20 minutes before the declared 16:20 BRT / 19:20 UTC cutoff. The official minutes were therefore already public. They also contain directly relevant financial-stability evidence: staff and participants discussed rapid growth in AI-related debt, off-balance-sheet leasing commitments, circular financing and the possibility of losses if AI investment returns disappoint. Sources: https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20261118a.htm and https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomcminutes20261028.htm
issues.required_correction: Remove the false statement that the FOMC minutes were still beyond the cutoff from both editions and all pending metadata. Add the official release and minutes to the references, distinguish the staff assessment from participants' views, and incorporate the relevant AI-financial-stability evidence without presenting a stress scenario as a realized loss. Re-evaluate the information-cutoff watch list and conclusion.

issues.evidence: Both editions state that the UK unemployment rate of 4.6% in July–September 2026 was down from 4.7% in the previous rolling quarter. The cited ONS November 2026 labour-market release states that 4.6% was down by 0.3 percentage points on the latest quarter, implying a previous-quarter rate of 4.9%, not 4.7%. The comparison is inconsistent with the cited primary source. Source: https://www.ons.gov.uk/employmentandlabourmarket/peopleinwork/employmentandemployeetypes/bulletins/uklabourmarket/november2026
issues.required_correction: Replace the 4.7% comparison in both languages with the ONS-reported 0.3 percentage-point quarterly decline, or state the implied 4.9% previous-quarter rate. Preserve the July–September reference period and the distinction from provisional October payroll data.

issues.evidence: The SEC S-1/A does not describe the $900.9 billion aggregate as uniformly firm, unconditional obligations. It says approximately $186.2 billion is subject to exercisable termination rights or contingent conditions before commencement; approximately $150–175 billion of additional compute/infrastructure payments under arrangements without fixed dollar commitments are excluded from the $900.9 billion; and $4.2 billion of the $70.7 billion expected within 12 months is subject to contingent conditions or termination rights. The current wording mentions different legal forms and maturities but omits these material qualifications, overstating the firmness and completeness of the headline commitment stock. Sources: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2130357/000162828026074338/anthropicpbc-sx1ax3.htm (Contractual Obligations, approximately lines 14601–14713)
issues.required_correction: Separate fixed/determinable obligations, commitments subject to termination or conditions, short-term and subsequent commitments, and additional arrangements without fixed dollar amounts. Qualify the $70.7 billion near-term amount with its $4.2 billion conditional/terminable component, and identify the $150–175 billion excluded estimate separately. Keep incurred expense, cash paid, contractual obligation, conditional commitment and prospective capacity distinct in both languages.

issues.evidence: The cited Reuters report distinguishes several events and actors: Iranian drones struck a US military radar system in Bahrain; a ship in the Strait of Hormuz was hit twice; the US carried out airstrikes on Iran; and the Houthis claimed five drones toward two Saudi pipeline pumping stations. The draft compresses these into generic 'reported attacks' in the Strait and wider Gulf without identifying actors or separating reported events from a party's claim. This leaves the geographic and actor attribution ambiguous in a report classified with war and armed-conflict phenomena. Source: https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/oil-slips-supply-surplus-outlook-despite-gulf-tensions-2026-11-17/
issues.required_correction: Attribute the relevant incidents to the actors and source, distinguish Reuters-reported events from Houthi claims, and avoid implying that every event occurred in the Strait or that a sustained closure has been established. Retain the limitation that attack reports do not prove a lasting route interruption.

issues.evidence: Reference [13] points to the Senate's generic plenary-session page, not to the specific Senate notice supporting the rescheduled 18 November vote, four pending floor highlights and the Executive's estimate of up to R$56 billion in 2027 primary-balance improvement. The official Senate notice published 17 November directly supports those claims. The English text also translates 'destaques' as 'amendments', which is not equivalent to the source's description of four pending highlights. Source: https://www12.senado.leg.br/noticias/materias/2026/11/17/votacao-de-destaques-ao-ajuste-fiscal-e-remarcada-na-quarta-feira
issues.required_correction: Replace reference [13] in both editions with the claim-specific Agência Senado notice. In English, describe the four items as pending floor highlights or highlighted provisions, not amendments. Preserve the R$56 billion figure as an Executive estimate conditional on legislative approval and implementation.
